title: Understanding Bandwidth in KDE
text: The bandwidth in a Kernel Density Estimate (KDE) controls the smoothness of the resulting plot. A larger bandwidth can cause the plot to appear smoother, potentially masking the true distribution of the data. Consider how this might affect a multimodal distribution.

title: Effect of Large Bandwidth
text: When the bandwidth is too large, it can cause distinct peaks in the data to merge into a single peak, making a multimodal distribution appear unimodal. Think about how this could make a distribution look like a normal distribution.

hintAnswer: It becomes overly smooth, potentially hiding multiple peaks.
title: Identifying the Issue
text: What happens to the appearance of a KDE plot when the bandwidth is too large?
choices: It becomes overly smooth, potentially hiding multiple peaks.
It becomes too jagged, showing too many peaks.
